open_points.subject: canonical_bytes error reporting
open_points.text: “with a reason naming the first offending item in text order”
open_points.question: What exact reason text must NonCanonicalValueError carry for each failure, and how is an offending syntax location, duplicate member, number, or string to be named?
options: Use fixed reason templates with offsets or paths
Use parser-produced messages
Use short category-only messages
open_points.default_guess: Use deterministic category-specific messages containing a JSON path when available and a character offset for syntax errors.

open_points.subject: canonical_bytes failure precedence
open_points.text: “the first offending item in text order”
open_points.question: When malformed syntax and a semantic violation such as a duplicate name, non-finite token, unsafe integer, or lone surrogate coexist, how is textual precedence determined and which error wins?
options: Report whichever violation is encountered first by a single left-to-right parser
Complete syntax parsing first, then report semantic violations
Use the standard parser's failure precedence
open_points.default_guess: Use a single left-to-right parse and report the earliest detectable violation by source position.

open_points.subject: canonical_bytes numeric input model
open_points.text: “numbers written in the ECMAScript shortest round-trip form” and “when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1)”
open_points.question: How should finite fraction-or-exponent tokens that overflow binary64, underflow, or round to a different value be handled, and is the safe-integer restriction intentionally inapplicable when the same mathematical integer is written with a fraction or exponent?
options: Apply RFC 8785 binary64 conversion and reject only non-finite results; apply the safe-integer rule only to lexical integers
Reject every token whose exact decimal value is not exactly representable as binary64
Apply the safe-integer rule to every mathematically integral value regardless of spelling
open_points.default_guess: Apply binary64 conversion, reject non-finite results, and apply the stated safe-integer bound only to tokens with neither fraction nor exponent.

open_points.subject: content_identity subject dispatch
open_points.text: “IdentitySubject: imported runtime symbol; no local surface details available”
open_points.question: What are the exhaustive runtime alternatives of IdentitySubject, and what must happen if a value is not an instance of one of the nine named content models?
options: The named models are exhaustive and an unknown value raises TypeError
Dispatch by subject_kind and reject unknown tags
Assume runtime validation makes an unknown value impossible
open_points.default_guess: Treat the named models as exhaustive, dispatch by concrete type, and raise TypeError for an unknown value.

open_points.subject: content_identity nested PortRef serialization
open_points.text: “PortRef: imported runtime symbol; no local surface details available” and “with nested models as objects keyed by field name”
open_points.question: Which concrete models can occur as PortRef values in TrialCaseContent, and is the listed set JsonPayload, FileFactsRef, SpooledFilesRef, and StoredValuesRef exhaustive?
options: Those four listed reference models are exhaustive
PortRef has additional variants not described here
The runtime object supplies its own serialization
open_points.default_guess: Assume the four listed reference models are the exhaustive PortRef variants.

open_points.subject: content_identity embedded canonical_json
open_points.text: “with nested models as objects keyed by field name” and “JSON-text fields such as value_schema kept as JSON strings”
open_points.question: When a nested JsonPayload occurs in TrialCaseContent, should its canonical_json bytes become the JSON value they encode, a UTF-8 text string, or another byte representation in the identity object?
options: Embed the decoded JSON value
Embed the UTF-8 JSON text as a string
Encode the bytes as hexadecimal or base64
open_points.default_guess: Embed the decoded JSON value, matching the explicit idempotency-key treatment.

open_points.subject: content_identity canonical_json validation
open_points.text: “holding the JSON value its canonical_json encodes” and “MUST let NonCanonicalValueError from canonical_bytes propagate unchanged when any JSON text the subject carries cannot be represented canonically”
open_points.question: Are canonical_json byte fields guaranteed to contain valid UTF-8 JCS bytes, or must content_identity decode, parse, canonicalize, and reject invalid or merely non-canonical bytes; and what exception applies to invalid UTF-8?
options: Trust canonical_json as a model invariant
Parse and canonicalize any valid UTF-8 JSON, rejecting invalid data with NonCanonicalValueError
Require the bytes already equal their canonical re-encoding
open_points.default_guess: Decode as UTF-8, parse and canonicalize the represented value, and translate invalid UTF-8 or JSON into NonCanonicalValueError.

open_points.subject: content_identity idempotency_key duplicate ports
open_points.text: “one JSON object with one member per entry of fields, named by the entry's port”
open_points.question: What happens when two JsonPayload entries have the same port name?
options: Reject duplicate ports
Keep the first entry
Keep the last entry
Allow duplicate object members until canonical_bytes rejects them
open_points.default_guess: Reject duplicate port names with NonCanonicalValueError.

open_points.subject: content_identity unordered-list ties
open_points.text: “ports by (direction, name), flow nodes by node_id, flow edges by (to_node, to_port, from_node, from_port), flow constants by (to_node, to_port)”
open_points.question: If two elements have the same specified sort key but differ in other fields, should their original order remain identity-significant, should further fields break the tie, or should such duplicates be rejected?
options: Use a stable sort and retain input order for ties
Add a complete canonical tie-breaker from all fields
Reject repeated sort keys
open_points.default_guess: Use the specified keys exactly with a stable sort, leaving tied elements in their original order.

open_points.subject: content_identity port sorting scope
open_points.text: “ports by (direction, name)”
open_points.question: Are each variant's inputs and outputs sorted independently in their existing fields, or are all ports combined, sorted, and then divided again?
options: Sort each inputs or outputs tuple independently
Combine all ports before sorting
Only sort a list when it can contain both directions
open_points.default_guess: Sort every port-containing field independently.

open_points.subject: fit_port_value reasons
open_points.text: “a reason naming the port and, for a list, the failing element index”
open_points.question: What exact reason strings must be returned for presence, carriage, schema, and size failures, including malformed schema or candidate JSON?
options: Fixed templates per failure
Free-form deterministic explanations
Only include the port name and optional index
open_points.default_guess: Use fixed deterministic templates containing the port name, check name, and top-level list index when applicable.

open_points.subject: fit_port_value candidate dispatch
open_points.text: “PortCandidate: imported runtime symbol; no local surface details available”
open_points.question: Are JsonCandidate, FileCandidate, and FileListCandidate the exhaustive candidate variants, and how should an unknown runtime value be classified without reflective probing?
options: Treat the three listed classes as exhaustive and classify unknown values as carriage failure
Raise for a value outside the declared union
Dispatch using candidate_kind rather than concrete type
open_points.default_guess: Dispatch by the three concrete classes and return a carriage failure for anything else.

open_points.subject: fit_port_value canonical_json invariant
open_points.text: “the candidate's canonical_json”
open_points.question: Must fit_port_value verify that canonical_json is valid UTF-8 and already in JCS canonical form, merely parse any well-formed JSON bytes, or trust the field's name as an enforced model invariant?
options: Trust it as already canonical
Accept any well-formed UTF-8 JSON without checking canonical spelling
Require exact JCS canonical bytes
open_points.default_guess: Trust canonicality but catch decoding or parsing failures and return a schema failure.

open_points.subject: fit_port_value schema document parsing
open_points.text: “The schema check of a value port parses the port's value_schema” and “a schema that is not a JSON object or uses any other keyword ... fits no value”
open_points.question: Do duplicate object names, non-finite tokens, lone surrogates, or unsafe integers in value_schema make the schema invalid under canonical_bytes rules, ordinary strict JSON rules, or some other rules?
options: Apply all canonical_bytes validation rules
Require ordinary strict JSON only
Trust value_schema as prevalidated
open_points.default_guess: Parse with the same strict JSON-value rules as canonical_bytes and treat any failure as a schema-check failure.

open_points.subject: fit_port_value schema meta-validation
open_points.text: “Supported schema keywords are only type ... enum ... const ... properties and required ... additionalProperties ... items ... minItems, maxItems, minLength, maxLength, minimum and maximum”
open_points.question: What shapes and bounds are valid for each keyword—for example, whether properties values and items must be schema objects, required must contain distinct strings, limits must be non-negative integers, and minimum or maximum must be finite numbers—and what happens when these constraints are violated?
options: Use the corresponding JSON Schema meta-schema constraints and fail invalid schemas
Coerce or ignore malformed keyword values
Only enforce the few shapes explicitly stated
open_points.default_guess: Apply the conventional JSON Schema type constraints to every supported keyword and make any malformed keyword value fail the schema check.

open_points.subject: fit_port_value schema keyword applicability
open_points.text: “Supported schema keywords are only ...”
open_points.question: When a supported keyword is used with an inapplicable instance type or without a matching type keyword, is it ignored as in JSON Schema, does it make the schema invalid, or does it make the instance fail?
options: Follow JSON Schema applicability rules
Treat the schema as invalid
Treat every instance as failing that keyword
open_points.default_guess: Follow standard JSON Schema applicability rules.

open_points.subject: fit_port_value empty schema and defaults
open_points.text: “a schema that is not a JSON object or uses any other keyword ... fits no value”
open_points.question: Does an empty schema object match every value, and do omitted properties, required, additionalProperties, and items use normal JSON Schema defaults, especially additionalProperties=true?
options: Use normal JSON Schema defaults and let an empty object match all values
Require type and reject an empty schema
Use closed objects unless additionalProperties is explicitly true
open_points.default_guess: Use normal JSON Schema defaults: an empty object matches all values and additional properties are allowed by default.

open_points.subject: fit_port_value properties semantics
open_points.text: “properties and required for objects, additionalProperties given as true or false only”
open_points.question: Must properties named in properties be validated whenever present, how are required names not listed in properties handled, and does additionalProperties=false reject every key absent from properties?
options: Use standard JSON Schema object semantics
Require required names also to appear in properties
Treat properties only as an allow-list
open_points.default_guess: Use standard JSON Schema object semantics.

open_points.subject: fit_port_value enum and const equality
open_points.text: “enum (non-empty array of distinct scalars), const (one scalar)”
open_points.question: What equality relation defines distinctness and matching, particularly for 1 versus 1.0 and for true versus 1?
options: Use JSON Schema equality where numerically equal numbers match but booleans and numbers differ
Use representation-sensitive equality
Use Python equality
open_points.default_guess: Use JSON semantic equality: 1 and 1.0 match, while true and 1 do not.

open_points.subject: fit_port_value integer and numeric comparison
open_points.text: “integer means a number without a fraction” and “minimum and maximum”
open_points.question: Does integer mean a mathematically integral parsed number or a token whose original spelling has no decimal point or exponent, and are minimum or maximum comparisons performed on binary64 values or exact decimal values?
options: Use mathematical integrality and binary64 values
Use lexical spelling and exact decimal comparison
Use mathematical integrality and exact decimal comparison
open_points.default_guess: Use mathematical integrality of the parsed binary64 number and compare binary64 values.

open_points.subject: fit_port_value string length
open_points.text: “minLength, maxLength”
open_points.question: Is string length counted in Unicode code points, UTF-16 code units, or UTF-8 bytes?
options: Unicode code points
UTF-16 code units
UTF-8 bytes
open_points.default_guess: Count Unicode code points, following JSON Schema semantics.

open_points.subject: fit_port_value nested list failures
open_points.text: “within one check the elements of a list are judged in list order and the reason names the index of the first failing element”
open_points.question: Does this apply only to the top-level cardinality-many candidate and file list, or also to arrays recursively validated through items; if recursive, how must a nested index path be reported?
options: Only report the top-level candidate index
Report a full nested index path
Report only the innermost failing index
open_points.default_guess: Report the top-level cardinality-many index; nested array traversal is ordered but does not require a full path.

open_points.subject: fit_port_value empty cardinality-many candidate
open_points.text: “for cardinality many the candidate MUST be a JSON array and every element MUST fit the schema” and “a file port of cardinality many receives a file_list candidate”
open_points.question: Do empty JSON arrays and empty file lists fit cardinality many when no schema minItems constraint rejects the JSON array?
options: Yes, many permits zero elements
No, many means one or more
JSON arrays may be empty but file lists may not
open_points.default_guess: Allow empty arrays and file lists; per-element checks then pass vacuously.
